prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational, edit an existing scientific manuscript concept illustration.
Input image is the edit target. Preserve the clean white background, navy/teal/ochre palette, central laboratory apparatus and independent-evaluator separation. Keep a polished publication figure, legible at full page width.
Replace the title with "Abductive inquiry in ChemWorld".
Upper half: Autonomous researcher at left exchanges "Choose experiments" and "Receive observations" with a central "Programmable chemical world". Right: "Independent evaluation" containing "Hidden world laws" and "Withheld outcomes", connected only to the world. No arrow sends private truth to the researcher. Retain chemical reaction vessel, separation flask, crystals. Simplify tiny labels to avoid clutter.
Redesign the lower half as five equal connected cards in a horizontal loop, with the exact headings:
"Observations" -> "Candidate explanations" -> "Testable expectations" -> "Experiments" -> "Revision".
Under each heading use exactly one short line respectively:
"What needs explaining?"
"What could account for it?"
"What should follow?"
"What actually happens?"
"What remains supported?"
Use simple illustrations in the cards (assay trace, two hypothesis sheets, predicted curve, flask, revised notebook). Above the link from Observations to Candidate explanations put the small label "Abduction"; above Candidate explanations to Testable expectations put "Deduction"; above Experiments to Revision put "Empirical evaluation". A clear curved return arrow from Revision back to Candidate explanations labelled "Continue inquiry". Include a smaller outward branch from Revision labelled "Predictions under new interventions" without implying guaranteed correctness. No Einstein portrait, no historical timeline, no numerical data, no claim of a measured private mind or universally correct discovery.
Bottom tiny footer exact: "Concept illustration; observable research records, not private cognition".
Landscape composition around 3:2, generous whitespace, consistent typography, no overlaps.
